policies.title: Uruguay: named ordinary passports visa-free
policies.summary: The Ministry of Interior’s current common-passport schedule expressly marks these passport issuers as not needing a visa for temporary admission. This is a visa-free baseline, not an eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route.
conditions: The schedule is limited to the ordinary/common-passport column. Passport type, purpose, activity and duration footnotes remain applicable.

For South Korea, Dominica, Guyana, Latvia, Russia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, the no-visa treatment is tourist-only or subject to prior consultation for work or stays beyond the stated period; this candidate records only the short visitor baseline.

Malaysia has 30-day temporary admission without a visa. Hong Kong is covered only for passports marked HKSAR, which directly matches the catalog’s HKSAR passport. Macao is expressly exempt for its common passport and travel document.

No eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route is identified by the cited nationality schedule. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, third-country-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Uruguay: named and explicit-residual ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: The current Ministry of Interior schedule expressly marks these ordinary passports as needing a visa or, for passport issuers not in its named exemption list, applies its explicit rule that the remaining countries need a visa. The normalized baseline is visa_required: the official process is consular and advance, not eVisa or visa on arrival.
conditions: The schedule footnote says these marked (5) require prior authorization. The policy remains visa_required whether the authority labels the advance route as prior authorization or consular visa.

Palestine’s ordinary-passport row says admission is granted with prior consultation; the Foreign Ministry’s current prior-consultation process is a consular visa process, so it is likewise normalized as visa_required.

The Foreign Ministry says a tourist-visa applicant must request a consular interview in advance; after authorization the visa is stamped in the passport. An appointment, form, document upload or processing inquiry is not an eVisa.
Taiwan’s row says a travel certificate has been required since 5 December 2018; this does not establish a visa-free, eVisa or visa-on-arrival route.

The schedule lists conditional visa exemptions for specified Dominican and PRC passport holders with valid third-country visas and port restrictions. Those conditional third-country-document routes are excluded and do not alter this nationality-only baseline.
Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, refugee, stateless, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.
